newsitem.title: POLAND: Price curb cut 96 profit at Polish Plock refinery.
newsitem.headline: Price curb cut 96 profit at Polish Plock refinery.

text.p: Net profits of Poland's largest oil refiner, Petrochemia Plock SA, fell to 217 million zlotys in 1996 from 476 million in 1995, due to rigid government fuel price controls, the firm's president said on Monday.

Announcing the preliminary figures at a news conference, Konrad Jaskola said last year's profits would have been much higher had the government freed prices of fuels earlier than it eventually did -- on February 14 of this year.
"We expect that net profit this year will reach about 70 percent of the 1995 level, that is about 300 million zlotys," Jaskola later told reporters.
"We estimate that, from April 1996 to February 1997, the profit lost due to fixed fuel prices amounted to $150 million," Jaskola told the conference.
He said the refinery's revenue from sales totalled 9.9 billion zlotys in 1996, compared with 8.7 billion in 1995.
Gross profit last year was 346 million zlotys against 786 million in 1995.

In 1996 Petrochemia Plock processed 10.3 million tonnnes of crude oil. It expects its investments in the next two years to boost its crude processing capacity from an expected 10.5 million tonnes this year to 12.6 million in 2000.
It also expects its production of petrol and diesel fuel to rise from an expected 6.5 million tonnes in 1997 to 8.7 million tonnes after the investment programme is completed in 1999.
The refinery has a 75 percent share of Poland's crude oil processing, 66 percent of national fuels production, and it supplies 57 percent of the liquid fuels used in the country.
